scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to sell their former roommate's video games after the roommate left without settling their stuff. Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: The roommate moved out without paying the last bit of rent and left some stuff behind, including 60 video games. The landlord's place has a rule where if you don't take your stuff, they'll charge you to have someone remove it, which can be expensive. The person in question tried to contact the roommate for two weeks to pick up the stuff or take it to the dump, but the roommate didn't respond. So, they took most of the stuff to the dump but decided to sell the video games, making $600 from a local store. Now, the roommate found out and is upset, calling them an asshole and asking for the money back. Legally, there's nothing the roommate can do, but the person is wondering if they're in the wrong. Alright, so I need to think about the ethical implications here. Is it okay to sell someone else's property when they've abandoned it, especially when they're not responding to your attempts to contact them? On one hand, the roommate left without paying the last rent and didn't take their stuff, which could have cost the person money if the landlord had to dispose of it. Selling the games seems like a way to recover some of that loss. On the other hand, the games belong to the roommate, and selling them without permission might be seen as taking advantage of the situation. I should also consider the intent. Did the person intend to keep the money for themselves, or were they trying to mitigate their own financial loss? If they were trying to cover the costs that the roommate's actions might have caused, that might be seen differently than if they were just trying to profit from someone else's belongings. Another angle is the communication aspect. The person tried to contact the roommate for two weeks, which shows they made an effort to handle the situation responsibly. The roommate's lack of response could be seen as abandonment, which might give the person more justification in dealing with the property as they saw fit. But then, even if the roommate abandoned the stuff, selling it without their consent might still be crossing a line. Property rights are important, and even if someone abandons something, it doesn't automatically transfer ownership. The person could have donated the games or stored them safely instead of selling them for personal gain. Also, the emotional aspect comes into play. The roommate got upset when they found out, which indicates that the person's actions affected their relationship negatively. Trust is crucial in roommate situations, and selling someone's belongings without their knowledge can definitely strain that trust. Legally, it seems like there's no issue, but ethically, it's a bit murkier. The person might feel justified in their actions to prevent financial loss, but others might see it as taking unfair advantage of the roommate's absence. In the end, it's a tough call. There are valid points on both sides. The person acted to protect their own interests, but they also disregarded the roommate's property rights. It might come down to whether the actions were proportionate and whether there were other options available besides selling the games.
